newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close lower as funds sell blue chips.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close lower as funds sell blue chips.

text.p: Program selling of blue chips by foreign institutions depressed the market for most of the day, traders said.
"There is some program selling by Japanese funds," said Ami Moris, vice president of dealing at Capitalcorp.

Added a Jardine Fleming salesman: "All the blue chips were hammered and they took down the index." He said some of the selling is linked to the redemption of money to make up for losses on the weakened Tokyo bourse.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended down 12.00 points lower to 1,220.38.
A wide range of heavyweights shed losses. Maybank, Tanjung, Tenaga, Resorts World and United Engineers lost between 20 and 40 cents.

Telekom fell 40 cents to 20.90 as part of the broad-based selling and renewed fears of competition in the phone industry, analysts said. Telecommunications stock TRI rebounded from early weakness to end 12 cents up at 5.10.
Small-capitalisation issues were resilient, with the Second Board index notching up 1.85 points to 608.86.
